chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who accumulates wealth. He said, 'He does not pay its zakat until a full year (hawl) passes over it.'

key_terms.يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ: a full year passes over it

ai.seo_question: When does the obligation of zakat begin on accumulated wealth according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the temporal condition for zakat on wealth, specifying that the obligation arises only after a complete lunar year (hawl) has passed over the accumulated amount. This ruling underscores the principle of *hawl* as a distinct prerequisite for zakat liability, distinguishing it from immediate dues like zakat on agricultural produce, and provides practical guidance for believers managing their financial obligations according to the Shia jurisprudential tradition.
